limitations: 489 games on 12 slate days (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-12): about two weeks of early-season play. Every interval here is wide and no result should be read as settled.
November-only, mostly non-conference schedule with many mismatches; first-half share, half correlations and tie rates may differ in conference play and in March.

The first three slates are forecast from the documented prior alone because no verified period score had been archived before those tips; several prior values (first-half share 0.47, independent halves, continuity factors 1.0) are this slice's assumptions, not owner-published numbers, and they were chosen by the author after the season had started.

The incumbent publishes no probability for first-half, team-total or overtime contracts, so against the incumbent the challenger adds coverage, not accuracy. Accuracy claims are only relative to a naive construction and to the Kalshi mid.

The Kalshi reference is a snapshot mid (two-sided, spread at most 10 cents) from the last capture before tip, typically minutes before tip, while the challenger uses a projection frozen hours earlier. A mid is not an executable fill; no fees, depth or slippage are modelled and nothing here is a betting result.
Kalshi lists first-half spread / total, team-total and overtime contracts for only a small subset of games, so those market comparisons rest on a few dozen games or fewer.
The incumbent's mean total and margin are taken as given, including its documented early-season scoring-level bias; that bias flows into first-half and team-total probabilities.

Scores are modelled with a normal approximation plus a re-weighted zero-margin cell; other key-number effects and skew in blowouts are not modelled. Second-half contracts are priced only as the remainder (final minus first half).
The synthetic all-games ladder is not a set of traded lines; rows inside a game are strongly dependent (handled by the game-cluster bootstrap) and the effective sample is the number of games.
Race-to-N and winning-margin-band contracts are not modelled. The raw Kalshi rules text was not read; contract meaning comes from the panel's parsed semantics.
Archive git history was not audited (depth-1 fetch); the prospective claim rests on in-file freeze timestamps and manifest hashes.

verdict.reason: 21 headline pooled Brier comparisons (Holm-adjusted): 0 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, 0 IMPROVED_NOT_VALIDATED, 2 NOT_IMPROVED, 19 INCONCLUSIVE. Favourable: none. Unfavourable: ['game_moneyline vs market:kalshi_mid', 'game_spread vs market:kalshi_mid']. The incumbent publishes no probability for first-half, team-total or overtime contracts, so the challenger's contribution there is COVERAGE with measured calibration, not an accuracy gain over the incumbent; any gain is over a naive construction, on about two weeks of November games, and the overall verdict stays INCONCLUSIVE unless every market-facing comparison is also favourable. The incumbent's full-game probabilities are retained.

limitations: Reference A0 is a re-implemented proxy of the incumbent's documented no-report participation rule, not the live frozen pf-1.3.0 forecasts, which live on data branches and were not read.

The incumbent reference on Kalshi tickers is the owner's walk-forward reproduction of nba-sim-0.1.0 (market_table_scored.p_data_only and prop_walk_forward_v3.p_sim); it has a 00:00 ET data cutoff and no injury report, so part of any challenger gain is information timing, and it uses regular-season history only.
Only one season (2025-26) of injury-report history exists: TRAIN and both TEST cohorts are from the same season, so there is no cross-season replication.

Kalshi candle mids are hourly candle-close quotes, not executable fills; candles were archived for a sample of events only, so the market comparison covers a minority of scored markets and may not be representative.

Kalshi lists props for players the venue expects to play, and yes/no settlement requires the player to enter the game; that population is selected on information the A0 arm does not have, and availability matters there only through minutes, not through the DNP hurdle.
No pregame starting-lineup data and no news feed are used; coach's-decision DNPs of unlisted players are invisible to the injury gate.

Injury-report rows are matched to player ids by the owner's archive (methods include matching against the game's own box-score roster); identity, not status, comes from that step. Unmatched rows cannot be applied.

Players returning from a long absence or newly acquired (not in the team's last 10 games) are outside the population; their minutes are handled only as a TRAIN-mean allowance in the 240-minute budget.
ESPN minutes are rounded to whole minutes per player; team minute sums therefore deviate from 240 by a few minutes.
Per-minute rates have no opponent, pace, rest or matchup adjustment; the conditional pmf treats minutes scenarios and the stat as independent given minutes.
Non-headline rows carry p_holm = 1.0 by construction and therefore read INCONCLUSIVE regardless of their confidence interval.
Fee-adjusted economics were not computed.

verdict.reason: Overall rule (fixed in code): VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT only if A2 is validated against the incumbent reproduction AND against the Kalshi T-60 mid in every prop family; better than the incumbent reproduction but not than the market reads IMPROVED_NOT_VALIDATED. Kalshi Brier, pooled TEST, A2 minus reference (negative = A2 better). Versus incumbent reproduction market_table_scored.p_data_only (both cohorts, about 100 games): player_points -0.0138 [-0.0206, -0.0069] n=2060 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT; player_rebounds -0.0163 [-0.0237, -0.0094] n=1892 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT; player_assists -0.0154 [-0.0252, -0.0057] n=1423 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT; player_threes -0.0121 [-0.0200, -0.0040] n=1274 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT. Versus the later incumbent reproduction prop_walk_forward_v3.p_sim (12 dates in cohort 2 only, non-headline): player_points -0.0079 [-0.0131, -0.0028] n=2296 INCONCLUSIVE; player_rebounds -0.0011 [-0.0063, +0.0040] n=2235 INCONCLUSIVE; player_assists -0.0102 [-0.0174, -0.0025] n=1750 INCONCLUSIVE; player_threes -0.0040 [-0.0082, +0.0005] n=1385 INCONCLUSIVE. Versus the Kalshi T-60 candle mid: player_points +0.0083 [+0.0037, +0.0127] n=2183 NOT_IMPROVED; player_rebounds +0.0021 [-0.0030, +0.0072] n=2054 INCONCLUSIVE; player_assists +0.0041 [-0.0017, +0.0099] n=1500 INCONCLUSIVE; player_threes -0.0017 [-0.0058, +0.0022] n=1306 INCONCLUSIVE. Versus the own no-report proxy A0 on the same ladders: player_points -0.0002 [-0.0008, +0.0004] n=16998 INCONCLUSIVE; player_rebounds +0.0010 [+0.0003, +0.0017] n=16845 INCONCLUSIVE; player_assists -0.0005 [-0.0012, +0.0001] n=13540 INCONCLUSIVE; player_threes -0.0002 [-0.0007, +0.0002] n=11345 INCONCLUSIVE. On Kalshi ladders (which settle yes/no only for players who entered the game) the availability features add nothing measurable over A0, so the gain over the incumbent reproduction comes from the base rate/minutes/dispersion model and its later information cutoff, not from the injury gate. Where the features do work is on the full rotation population: PIT injury gate ablation verdicts VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT; redistribution ablation verdicts VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, INCONCLUSIVE, VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT. The incumbent is retained: research-only evidence against reproduced references, not the live frozen forecasts, and no edge over the market mid is shown.

limitations: Fitted on NHL-API-derived outcomes (official scores, goalie game logs) whose source robots file says ai-train=no: flagged for the owner; rights tier UNRESOLVED_INTERNAL_ONLY, research only.

The Kalshi reference is the T-60 mid of the last two-sided candle; a mid is not an executable fill (no spread, fee or depth is charged), so being close to or better than it is not evidence of tradable edge.

Kalshi quotes cover the 2025 cohort only (one season, one cohort), so no market comparison can be 'replicated' under the pre-registered rule; totals and spreads are listed only from 2025-10-22 onward.

No KXNHLOVERTIME or KXNHLTEAMTOTAL market exists for the regular-season test games (overtime markets are playoff-only in the file; the team-total file is empty), so those families have no market reference.

MoneyPuck xG values come from MoneyPuck's own shot model, which is trained on history that may include later seasons; the per-game xG numbers are used as published (a mild look-ahead in the feature definition that the incumbent shares).

The incumbent probabilities are Monte-Carlo estimates (4,000 simulations per game), so part of any gap in the challenger's favour is incumbent simulation noise (about 0.008 s.d. per probability), not model skill.
Empty-net goals, score effects and pulled-goalie timing are handled only implicitly through the tie and one-goal-margin weights; there is no explicit endgame model.

No lineup, injury, travel or pregame-knowable starting-goalie information is used; ablation (d) is an ORACLE_NOT_PIT upper bound using the as-played starter and must not be read as an achievable gain.

Regular season only; playoff games (different overtime rules) are neither fitted nor evaluated. Hyper-parameters were chosen on one validation split (2019-2023), which includes the two COVID-shortened seasons.
Two test cohorts (1,312 games each) give limited power: differences of a few 1e-4 in log loss cannot be resolved, so INCONCLUSIVE rows are not evidence of equality.
Ablation variants are refitted with the headline hyper-parameters (not re-tuned), so ablation deltas are conditional on that choice.

verdict.reason: Headline = pooled 2024+2025 vs incumbent:DATA_ONLY_V1, 14 rows (7 families x logloss/brier), Holm-adjusted. VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT rows: 2 (families ['regulation_tie_overtime']); IMPROVED_NOT_VALIDATED: 0; NOT_IMPROVED: 0 (families []); INCONCLUSIVE: 12. Overall rule: VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT only if every headline log-loss row is validated and none is NOT_IMPROVED; mixed or partial evidence is reported as IMPROVED_NOT_VALIDATED (some validated/improved, none worse) or INCONCLUSIVE. Against the Kalshi T-60 mid (2025 cohort only, single cohort so never 'replicated'): challenger point estimate is worse than the market in 12 of 12 market rows; Holm-significantly worse in families []; CI entirely better than the market in []. The challenger does NOT beat the market.
